title: Naturality and evaluation equation for the coefficient Hom comparison
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $a,n\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme in its domain, and use the actual coefficient categories, tensor and internal Hom of [sk-def-sf-operations](i). Write $\mathbf1=\Lambda_X$, $H(P,M)=R\mathcal Hom_X(P,M)$ and $P^\vee=H(P,\mathbf1)$. The integral unit and tensor are completed; the field categories are the specified rationalization and common finite-stage categories, respectively. All tensor constraints and symmetries below are those of these categories, including their cohomological signs.

For $P,M$ in these categories, let $c_{P,M}:P^\vee\otimes M\to H(P,M)$ be the tensor--Hom transpose of
$$P^\vee\otimes M\otimes P\xrightarrow{1\otimes\sigma_{M,P}}P^\vee\otimes P\otimes M\xrightarrow{e_P\otimes1}\mathbf1\otimes M\cong M,$$
where $e_P:P^\vee\otimes P\to\mathbf1$ is coefficient evaluation. For morphisms $u:P\to P'$ and $v:M\to M'$, these specified maps satisfy
$$H(u,v)\circ c_{P',M}=c_{P,M'}\circ(u^\vee\otimes v).$$
Let $L,W$ be objects and $\gamma:L\xrightarrow{\sim}W$ an isomorphism. On any full subcategory on which every $c_{P,L}$ is invertible, put $D_WP=H(P,W)$ and $\theta_P=c_{P,L}^{-1}\circ H(P,\gamma^{-1})$. Then $\theta$ is natural contravariantly in $P$, and the actual evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_{P,W}:D_WP\otimes P\to W$ satisfies
$$\mathrm{ev}_{P,W}\circ(\theta_P^{-1}\otimes1_P)=\gamma\circ(e_P\otimes1_L)\circ(1_{P^\vee}\otimes\sigma_{L,P}).$$
Associators and unitors are inserted in the displayed composites. The statement concerns these evaluation-defined arrows, without an assumption on an exceptional inverse-image functor or an orientation. For perfect $P$ and $L=\Lambda_X(m)[s]$, $m,s\in\mathbf Z$, the comparison $c_{P,L}$ is invertible and its inverse is precisely the canonical isomorphism $H(P,\Lambda_X(m)[s])\xrightarrow{\sim}P^\vee(m)[s]$ of [sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange], using the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

proof.text:
On the stated full subcategory set $a_P=c_{P,L}$ and $h_P=H(P,\gamma^{-1})$. Both are invertible, the first by hypothesis and the second because $H(P,-)$ is a functor. Step 2 gives $H(u,1_L)a_{P'}=a_P(u^\vee\otimes1_L)$. Bifunctoriality gives $h_PH(u,1_W)=H(u,1_L)h_{P'}$. Multiplying these identities by $a_P^{-1}$ and $a_{P'}^{-1}$ proves
$$\theta_PH(u,1_W)=(u^\vee\otimes1_L)\theta_{P'}.$$
Also $\theta_P^{-1}=H(P,\gamma)a_P$. The covariant evaluation identity from Step 1 followed by its defining equation for $c$ now gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_{P,W}(\theta_P^{-1}\otimes1_P)
=\gamma\,\mathrm{ev}_{P,L}(c_{P,L}\otimes1_P)
=\gamma\,(e_P\otimes1_L)(1\otimes\sigma_{L,P}).$$
This is the displayed equation for the actual evaluation, for arbitrary $L,W$ and $\gamma$ subject only to the hypotheses in the statement.

By sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange this is invertible for dualizable P. Equality of inverse isomorphisms follows from this equality of their forward maps. Instantiate this generic argument for the four recorded closed domains, using precisely the membership witnesses of the shifted-line lemma.
